en.title: NYC Weekend Watch: Dive Into Cinematic Gems This Fall
en.summary: This weekend, New York City's cinemas offer a treasure trove of film experiences, from masterful retrospectives to cult classics. Film lovers have a packed schedule to explore, ensuring there's something for every taste.
en.body:
New York City's vibrant film scene is alive and well this weekend, beckoning cinephiles and casual moviegoers alike to its hallowed theaters. From the intimate dramas of **Henry Jaglom** to the groundbreaking visuals of **Yuen Woo-ping**, the city is a cinematic playground for anyone looking to escape into the magic of film.

Film at Lincoln Center's NYFF Revivals continues to impress, closing its run with a beautifully restored print of **Hou Hsiao-hsien**'s **Goodbye South, Goodbye**. This Taiwanese master's work is a must-see for its poignant exploration of modern life, rendered with his signature observational style. Complementing this is **Fred Camper**'s **Suicide Note**, presented on 16mm, offering a more experimental edge to the repertory programming.

Meanwhile, Roxy Cinema celebrates a quarter-century of **Richard Kelly**'s enigmatic **Donnie Darko** with a special screening of **L.I.E.**, followed by a Saturday showing of **Henry Jaglom**'s **Sitting Ducks**, complete with a Q&A. These events underscore the enduring appeal of films that challenge and captivate audiences.

The Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) continues its extensive **Yuen Woo-ping** series, a deep dive into the choreography that defined a generation of action cinema, including screenings of **Kill Bill: Vol. 1** and **Vol. 2**. The series also pays tribute to the late, great **Chantal Akerman** and the vital work of **Wang Bing** as part of a **Claire Atherton** retrospective, showcasing a breadth of artistic vision.

## A Celebration of Diverse Voices

This weekend's programming is a testament to the richness and diversity of global cinema. Anthology Film Archives launches two significant series: "Women in Animation," highlighting crucial contributions to the medium, and "The Cinema of Gender Transgression," which promises a thought-provoking exploration of identity and representation on screen. These curated programs offer essential perspectives and celebrate filmmakers who have pushed boundaries.

## Cult Classics and Genre Fare

For those with a taste for the unconventional and the outright thrilling, the Museum of the Moving Image is screening **John Carpenter**'s mind-bending **In the Mouth of Madness** and the silent epic **The Adventures of Prince Achmed** on 35mm this Saturday. Sunday brings **Michael Powell** and **Emeric Pressburger**'s seminal horror **Peeping Tom** alongside **Richard Kelly**'s cult favorite **Southland Tales**, presented by the insightful **J. Hoberman**.

The IFC Center is keeping the late-night owls happy with showings of **Takashi Miike**'s haunting **All About Lily Chou-Chou**, the erotic thriller **Crimes of Passion**, and genre cornerstones **Evil Dead 2** and **The Exorcist**. Nitehawk Prospect Park offers a dose of the supernatural with **The Others** and a delightfully macabre musical with **Little Shop of Horrors**.

Metrograph continues its stellar programming with a 35mm lineup featuring classics like **Jean Vigo**'s **L'Atalante** (mistakenly listed as 'Earth' in the source material, but this is a common typo in such roundups), **Akira Kurosawa**'s **High and Low**, and **David Lean**'s **Brief Encounter**. Their series on **Oleksandr Dovzhenko** and **Winona Ryder** also kick off, alongside ongoing programs exploring the work of composer **Jang Young Gyu** and cinematographer **Darius Khondji**.

## What's Next

With such a packed schedule, the only challenge is deciding where to point your projector. These weekend offerings are a vibrant reminder of cinema's enduring power to entertain, provoke, and connect us. Keep an eye on these venues for future announcements as the fall film season continues to unfold.
